case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption (Satya Narayana Tiwari and Anr. v. State of U.P.).

number_of_accused.reason: Two accused, husband and mother-in-law, are stated throughout the judgment.

accused_gender.quote: Only the husband and mother-in-law of the deceased have been accused of the offences in question.
accused_gender.reason: Accused include a female mother-in-law as well as a male husband; 'Male' alone is contradicted.

accused_age.quote: The deceased was aged about 24 years
accused_age.reason: The age of 24 belongs to the deceased; no accused age is stated.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.correct_value: Husband ran a shop; occupation of mother-in-law not stated
accused_occupation.quote: her brother accused No. 1 - husband of the deceased had gone to his shop at about 8 P.M.
accused_occupation.reason: Judgment states the husband had a shop, so 'Not stated' is contradicted.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status of the accused is not stated in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record of the accused is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: The deceased is described as a young lady, a bride, so Female is supported.

victim_age.reason: Deceased is described as aged about 24 years.

victim_caste.reason: Victim caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Victim religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: Only the husband and mother-in-law of the deceased have been accused of the offences in question.
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Only the husband is a spouse; the mother-in-law is an in-law relative.

offence_category.reason: Case is a dowry death under s.304-B IPC.

statutory_provisions.reason: Headnote and judgment cite ss.304-B and 498-A IPC and s.4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

weapon.correct_value: Cloth ligature used for strangulation; kerosene used for burning
weapon.quote: It was the constricting material used by the accused for compressing the neck of the deceased.
weapon.reason: Judgment identifies a knotted cloth ligature and kerosene as the means used, not 'None mentioned'.

evidence_type.correct_value: Circumstantial; oral testimony of PW1 and PW2; medical (post mortem); recovery memos
evidence_type.quote: this case is also based on circumstantial evidence
evidence_type.reason: Omits oral testimony of PW1 and PW2, which the court relied on heavily.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused is mentioned in the judgment.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Dowry demand, persistent harassment, strangulation and burning are all highlighted by the court.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: The judgment does not discuss mitigating circumstances.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court acquitted the husband and mother-in-law.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court convicted both accused under ss.304-B, 498-A and DP Act s.4.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, so conviction stands.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Dowry death under s.304-B IPC; cruelty under s.498-A IPC; s.4 Dowry Prohibition Act
offence_finally_established.quote: The accused are established to have committed the offences under Sections 498-A and 304 B IPC and under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act
offence_finally_established.reason: Omits s.498-A IPC and s.4 Dowry Prohibition Act offences that were also established.

imprisonment_type.reason: High Court awarded life sentence under s.304-B IPC, which the Supreme Court upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life sentence has no stated term in years; null is appropriate.

fine_rs.reason: No fine amount is mentioned in the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: The accused, a husband and his mother-in-law, were charged in connection with the death of a bride who died of strangulation and burn injuries in her matrimonial home. The deceased, aged about 24, died within three years of marriage. The FIR alleged dowry demands for a Maruti car, which persisted after about six months of marriage. The mother-in-law lodged a report describing the death as suicide.
neutral_facts.quote: The accused are established to have committed the offences under Sections 498-A and 304 B IPC
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are largely accurate but state the court's guilt finding, which neutral facts must not reveal.

offence_severity.reason: High Court sentences of life, 3 years and 6 months rigorous imprisonment are stated in the judgment.

attempt_completion.reason: Death was caused, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.reason: Post mortem shows strangulation and superficial to deep burns.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Three (s.304-B IPC, s.498-A IPC, s.4 Dowry Prohibition Act)
number_of_offences.quote: The accused are established to have committed the offences under Sections 498-A and 304 B IPC and under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act
number_of_offences.reason: Judgment upholds three separate offences, not two.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss is recorded; dowry demand is not a loss value.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court states the crime was committed with preplanning and a false report was lodged.

motive.reason: Motive is the persistent demand for a Maruti car as dowry.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court accepted PW1/PW2 testimony, post mortem, recoveries and the cruelty evidence.

witness_credibility.reason: Court found PW1 and PW2 testimony credible regarding the Maruti car demand.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Surrender dates of 7.11.2000 and 13.11.2000 and the court's view on absconding are supported.

custody_duration.reason: No duration of custody is stated in the judgment.

bail_history.correct_value: Supreme Court granted bail on 27.10.2005; bail bonds later cancelled and accused ordered into custody
bail_history.quote: On 27.10.2005 this Court had granted bail to the appellants.
bail_history.reason: Judgment does state bail history, so 'Not stated' is contradicted.

trial_duration.correct_value: Not stated as a duration; dates: FIR 03.11.2000, High Court judgment 12.07.2005, Supreme Court decision 28.10.2010
trial_duration.quote: On 03.11.2000 an FIR was lodged by the father of the deceased
trial_duration.reason: Gives dates rather than a trial duration; the dates are supported but not a duration.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for appellants and respondent match the judgment's appearance list.

investigation_status.reason: Judgment states investigation was followed by a charge sheet and trial.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Failure to frame a s.302 IPC charge; trial judge wrongly treated non-production of the knot as against the prosecution
procedural_irregularity.quote: since no charge under Section 302 IPC was levelled, we cannot do so
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment identifies a missed s.302 charge and a trial judge error on the knot, contrary to 'None noted'.

appeal_history.reason: Acquittal by trial court, conviction by High Court and dismissal by Supreme Court are all supported.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Judgment does not record prosecution arguments; it reasons from prosecution evidence on cruelty, the Maruti car demand, and suicide being ruled out
prosecution_argument.quote: The prosecution has successfully proved the persistent demand of Maruti Car as a part of dowry by the two accused
prosecution_argument.reason: Substance matches the court's findings, but framed as prosecution argument, which the judgment does not record.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence argued suicide, alibi, Tabiz/depression theory, and that the proximity test was unmet; judgment does not record absence of direct evidence or a superfluous-approach argument
defence_argument.quote: The theory of suicide put forth by the defence completely falls through
defence_argument.reason: Suicide theory is supported, but 'absence of direct evidence' and the acquittal approach are misattributed.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Court applied the Kunhiabdulla ingredients of s.304-B and the soon-before proximity test.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Kunhiabdulla v. State of Kerala, 2004 (4) SCC 13; Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1980 SC 898
precedent_relied_upon.quote: as referred to in Bachan Singh Vs. State of Punjab, AIR 1980 SC 898
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Omits Bachan Singh, relied on for the rarest of rare point.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Life sentence under s.304-B upheld; death sentence not imposed because no s.302 charge was framed, though such cases fall in rarest of rare category
sentencing_rationale.quote: In fact, it was really a case under Section 302 IPC and death sentence should have been imposed in such a case, but since no charge under Section 302 IPC was levelled, we cannot do so
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale says the final sentence was imposed on rarest of rare grounds; the court did not impose death.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Judgment does not discuss mitigating factors; 'None' is an unbacked assertion.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court cites brutal barbaric nature, persistent dowry demand, cruelty, preplanning and at least two perpetrators.

other_sentence_order.reason: Bail bonds cancelled, custody ordered, and impleadment application allowed, per the judgment's final paragraphs.
